summary: Recorded the boundary execution and one refinement. CheckRun 13b5c712348f412eac6c7ce108a05d91 (exit 0, four cases) evaluated all seven comparisons completely: the four trim comparisons reproduce the finding (control holds; {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} and {1,3} violated with valid witnesses 3, 5, 7) and the three boundary comparisons hold — snapshot returns ok and moves the compacted index 0→1 in every trigger configuration where both trim calls made no progress, and is a no-op in the control because trim already compacted that index. I corrected the trim knowledge entry under its existing id so the 'snapshot remains available' caveat is measured rather than derived, appended the account with the measured boundary, and closed that question's discriminator. I also recorded a source-reasoned refinement of the runtime defect: because every message that could advance the origin's decided index is gated by the core's ballot check, the origin cannot observe a replacement at the assigned index while still promised to the assigning ballot, so the promise change always precedes the decided advance and the false `Ok` is delivered exactly when no tick runs between them — a one-round-trip window, consistent with the measured band. No execution was requested this turn (validation reports execution_requested false); both findings now rest on complete comparison chains with measured boundaries, leaving only same-cause variants and the unexercised follower-origin instance of the same window.
